_about: Reference lines for nebulae, shaded on the spectrum. Wavelengths are laboratory vacuum values (hydrogen lines follow from the Rydberg formula). The shaded width is SPHEREx's resolution at that wavelength (lambda / R), so a band shows where the line would land in SPHEREx data. It is not a detection. Person C: add paper references, as in data/features.json on the c/science branch.

glossary.hydrogen: Glowing hydrogen gas. Hot young stars strip electrons off hydrogen atoms, and the gas gives off these colours as the atoms recombine. Strong in emission and planetary nebulae.
glossary.h2: Hydrogen molecules heated by shock waves or ultraviolet light, common at the edges of star-forming clouds.
glossary.pah: Large carbon-rich molecules (polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) on tiny dust grains, glowing when starlight warms them.
